benchmark: Lygon Street, Carlton, Melbourne, inspiration only

executive_assessment.verdict: Evidence supports progressing Buono as a Sydney alpha concept, but not treating demand as proven for any address. Sandwiches are visibly competitive, pasta and salads have established fast-casual price anchors, and aperitivo can extend the day. The investment case remains location- and throughput-dependent.

market_envelope.meaning: Tourism can support CBD, beach and destination sites, but these totals do not identify food spend or Buono conversion.

market_envelope.meaning: Near-term category spending was positive, but it includes inflation, accommodation and all dining formats across NSW. It is not Sydney restaurant volume.

categories.name: Italian sandwiches and focaccia
categories.assessment: Strong current visibility and a validated willingness to pay, with clear crowd and expansion proxies. Competitive intensity and trend-fatigue risk are also high.

measured_price_band_aud.basis: current Diego & Co. schiacciate; other Sydney and interstate observations sit inside or near this range

demand_signals: Broadsheet reported in July 2025 that sandwiches had continued to soar and that new Sydney shops were opening to immediate crowds.
Good Ways expanded from Redfern to Alexandria and is described as having a cult following.
Current CBD Diego & Co. pricing reaches $25 for premium schiacciate.
risks: Editorial momentum is not transaction data.
Raineri queue evidence may reflect social-media novelty and capacity constraints as much as durable demand.
Google Trends direction is unknown because charts were not captured.
categories.model_implication: Treat focaccia as a hero acquisition product, but require a service-time gate and protect value with at least one entry sandwich below the premium $22-$25 tier.

categories.name: Fresh pasta and pasta bowls
categories.assessment: Established Sydney demand with both quick-service and more polished hybrids. Current accessible core pricing is roughly $20-$30, with premium handmade dishes above that.

measured_price_band_aud.basis: current IL BARETTO Newtown and The Italian Bowl core pasta menus

demand_signals: The Italian Bowl has traded in Newtown since 2005 and remains open seven days to 10pm or 11pm.
IL BARETTO opened a Newtown pasta bar in 2026 with takeaway bundles and noon-late trade.
Fabbrica operates a CBD pasta, sandwich, wine and retail hybrid daily to 10pm.
risks: Venue longevity and menu presence do not reveal unit sales.
Fresh pasta can be slower and more labour-intensive than the sandwich and salad dayparts.
A very short menu needs rotation discipline to preserve repeat appeal.
categories.model_implication: Use $22-$28 as the initial core single-pasta test corridor, with visible pan-to-bowl finishing and a measured ticket-time target. Premium proteins can sit above the core range.

sources.title: IL BARETTO Newtown, Pasta, Focaccia & Tiramisu

categories.name: Salads and complete meal bowls
categories.assessment: A mature adjacent fast-casual category with a strong network proof point. Buono's opportunity is an Italian flavour system, not the invention of salad bowls.

measured_price_band_aud.basis: current FISHBOWL regular and large core bowls; winter value box starts at $11.90

demand_signals: FISHBOWL reports 50+ Australian locations and names 18 Greater Sydney catchments.
The company states it has grown from a 26sqm Bondi site in 2016 to 60+ restaurants across Australia and New York.
Its current menu deliberately spans value boxes, regular bowls and large bowls.
risks: Brand network growth does not provide store-level profitability.
Italian side salads at $12-$18 are not automatically substitutes for a protein-complete lunch bowl.
A $25+ Buono salad would face strong value comparison with entrenched bowl chains.
categories.model_implication: Give every core salad complete-meal architecture and a base price at or below $22, with optional premium protein. Side salads can remain below $16.

categories.name: Aperitivo and day-to-night conversion
categories.assessment: Operationally validated by current Sydney venues, but highly sensitive to licence, frontage, ambience, local evening footfall and labour scheduling.

measured_price_band_aud.basis: current promotion and standard spritz observations across Bar Allora, Bloom, IL BARETTO and The Italian Bowl

demand_signals: Bloom explicitly switches from café to aperitivo at 3pm and publishes a 3-6pm menu.
Bar Allora runs aperitivo windows at 12-2pm and 4-6pm with sharp drink prices.
IL BARETTO Newtown integrates wine, spritz and beer into a noon-late pasta format.
risks: Presence of offers proves supply, not incremental profit.
Discounting can shift existing demand rather than create a new daypart.
The selected property must independently support evening safety, dwell time and alcohol licensing.
categories.model_implication: Model aperitivo as a separate daypart with its own conversion rate, beverage mix and staffing. Do not use lunch footfall as the evening demand base.

location_implications.critical_test: Prove that Buono adds value beyond existing delis through speed, seating, complete salads and evening hospitality, without relying on generic heritage claims.
Test whether stronger beverage and premium food prices offset rent and lower weekday lunch density.

lygon_benchmark.claim: Lygon Street's useful lesson is precinct layering: restaurants, gelato, cafés, bars, retail, residents, students and tourists create reasons to visit across the day.
lygon_benchmark.translation_to_sydney: Copy the rhythm and legibility, not the geography or an old-school restaurant strip. Buono should create a small precinct effect inside one tenancy through bakery theatre, takeaway, seated meals, wine and a visible daypart change.

unknowns: No site-level pedestrian counts or conversion rates have yet been measured.
No competitor transaction counts, sales mix, repeat rate or unit economics are public in the reviewed sources.
Google Trends directional and index observations remain unknown pending manual chart capture.
Raineri's current primary menu, price and hours were not accessible.
Alcohol licence feasibility, outdoor seating, acoustic limits and evening safety are property-specific and outside this market pack.
The claim that sandwiches are at or near peak cannot be confirmed quantitatively. It should be treated as a saturation risk hypothesis.
